title: Knicks Pull Off the Biggest Comeback in NBA Finals History!
summary: Have you ever seen a team look totally beaten, only to fight back and win? That's exactly what happened Wednesday night at Madison Square Garden. The New York Knicks were losing by 29 points to the San Antonio Spurs in Game 4 of the NBA Finals. It seemed like the game was over. But the Knicks didn't give up. They made the biggest comeback in Finals history and won 107-106! OG Anunoby tipped in a missed shot with just 1.2 seconds left to seal the victory. The Knicks now lead the series 3-1 and are just one win away from their first championship in over 50 years. Jalen Brunson led the charge with 36 points, and Anunoby added 33. The Spurs had a huge first half, led by Victor Wembanyama's 24 points and 13 rebounds. But in the second half, the Knicks' defense clamped down, and the Spurs' shots stopped falling. The crowd went wild, singing 'Don't Stop Believin'' after the game. No team had ever come back from more than 24 points down in a Finals game before. The Knicks beat that record by five points! Game 5 is Saturday in San Antonio. Can the Knicks finish the job?
why_it_matters: This shows that no matter how far behind you feel, hard work and believing in yourself can still lead to an amazing success.
